sources.title: Tree protection and planning
sources.verified_claim: Enfield publishes TPO location data and states protected-tree works require consent; development planning must consider tree protection and may require supporting tree documentation.

sources.title: Heritage
sources.verified_claim: Enfield distinguishes designated and non-designated heritage assets and uses heritage significance as part of planning assessment; asset status must be checked site by site.

sources.title: Historic parks and landscapes
sources.verified_claim: Enfield states development affecting registered parks, gardens or locally significant landscapes must consider their special character and conservation; this is not evidence that a sample parcel intersects one.

sources.title: Conservation areas
sources.verified_claim: Havering has 11 conservation areas and states their contribution is a material consideration, with additional controls including tree and Article 4 restrictions in some areas.

sources.title: Listed buildings
sources.verified_claim: Havering states listed-building consent is required for changes affecting special interest and planning decisions balance historic significance against function, condition and viability.

sources.title: Local Heritage List
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's local heritage list includes archaeology, buildings and designed landscapes; local listing adds no separate consent regime but is a material consideration in planning decisions.

sources.title: Statutory listed buildings
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth states statutory listed buildings are protected by law and works affecting them can require Listed Building Consent; exact listing status remains site specific.

sources.title: Advice for listed buildings and conservation areas
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth offers heritage pre-application advice on listed buildings and conservation areas; advice may improve proposals but is not permission or a guarantee of acceptance.
